topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: The Library vs. The Filing Cabinet
lecture_lines: Transformers have two distinct memory types.
Attention is your working memory.
The MLP acts as long-term memory.
MLPs store facts in synaptic weights.
It is like a internal brain database.
animations: Display two boxes: 'Attention' (left) and 'MLP' (right) with labels.
Animate 'Attention' as a flickering [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/spotlight.svg] over scattered text blocks.
Animate 'MLP' as a static, glowing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cabinet.svg] with fixed patterns.
Show the 'Attention' box fading in intensity while the 'MLP' becomes solid and vibrant.
Highlight both labels, establishing them as the 'Working' and 'Static' memory using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/database.svg] icon to represent structured storage.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Neuron as a Pattern Matcher
lecture_lines: A neuron acts as a pattern matcher.
It detects specific features in data.
Weights determine the neuron's sensitivity.
animations: Display an Input Vector (green, #00FF00) approaching a node labeled 'Neuron' represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg].
Show a Weight Matrix (blue, #0000FF) interacting with the Input Vector at the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg].
Animate the 'Neuron' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] flashing bright yellow (#FFFF00) when the pattern matches.

sections.title: Mechanism: Key-Value Memory Networks
lecture_lines: MLPs function as Key-Value memories.
Keys detect the incoming input prompt.
Values project the specific output answer.
This bridges prompts to factual answers.
Like a lock finding its key.
animations: Display the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg] interacting with a 'Prompt' vector, causing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lock.svg] to open.
Show the Value vector being projected into a space, resulting in the label 'Paris'.

sections.title: Visualization: The Fact-Retrieval Process
lecture_lines: Information flows through the network layers.
Weights activate to match patterns.
Facts emerge from these weight connections.
Retrieval is a distributed process.
Not one neuron holds the fact.
animations: Display a chain of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] nodes: Input Token -> MLP Layer -> Output Token.
Animate pulses moving through the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] nodes within the MLP Layer.
Highlight multiple connections spreading throughout the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] layer to show 'distributed' storage.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
lecture_lines: MLPs are vast distributed databases.
Training saves facts into weights.
We can surgically update these weights.
animations: Visualize the MLP as a vast, 3D grid of weights (dots).
Show a 'surgical' edit on a specific cluster of weights using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scalpel.svg] (changing color).
Final overlay: 'MLP: A Distributed Knowledge Base'.
